claims.text: The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide teaches users to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi, use any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs, import and use Terraform modules directly, convert HCL to Pulumi, and orchestrate Terraform and Pulumi deployments together.
Any Terraform provider can be used in Pulumi programs.
Terraform modules can be imported and used directly in Pulumi.
pulumi.StackReference takes a stack name and getOutput retrieves a stack output; "core-infra" is used as a StackReference name (fully qualified name normally org/project/stack).

The Pulumi Terraform provider exposes a `terraform.state.S3Reference` resource (in @pulumi/terraform) taking `bucket` and `key` arguments to reference Terraform state stored in S3, with a `getOutput` method.
`S3Reference` is accessible as `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` from the `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` import.
The aws.ecs.Cluster resource accepts a `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` argument with `kmsKeyId` and `logging` properties, with logging value "DEFAULT".
`pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
The `pulumi import` command syntax takes a resource type token (e.g. aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc), a name, and a resource ID, as in `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`.
Pulumi supports transferring state ownership gradually, resource-by-resource, when migrating from Terraform.
A Pulumi import API exists that can be used programmatically within a program to import resources.
Pulumi policies (CrossGuard/Policy as Code) can enforce infrastructure policies across both Terraform and Pulumi resources.
The @pulumi/policy package exports PolicyPack and validateResourceOfType, and policies accept name, description, enforcementLevel "mandatory", and validateResource fields.
aws.s3.Bucket has an `acl` property that can be "public-read" or "public-read-write".
Automation API allows embedding Pulumi in applications for dynamic infrastructure management.
The Automation API exposes LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack with stackName, projectName, and program options; stack.setConfig(key, {value}) and stack.up({onOutput}) returning result with `outputs`.
Component resources can integrate with Terraform behind the scenes, leaving the complexity of multi-tool management to the platform team rather than development teams.
pulumi.ComponentResource is extended with super(type, name, {}, opts) and registerOutputs is called to register outputs.
